🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-11-18 23:00 → 2026-11-19 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **A research integration loop closed** — earlier review branches were merged onto the frozen core, giving the research line one current base to build on. [commit 4b6d7ef](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/commit/4b6d7ef9aabd23932668711ee1d6cf774d9844d7)

> **A comparison was rescued before it started** — a model, context, and hardware mismatch surfaced ahead of the head-to-head and was acknowledged as the kind of gap that would have quietly distorted the result. [tg:tawg:6445]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### verifiable-execution-claim-authorization
_The research line moved from scattered branches to a merged, documented baseline._

- Pavlo **Merged** the integration that brought the earlier research branches onto the frozen ERC-8404 core, so reviewers can work from one current base instead of reconciling stale forks. [PR #14](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/14)
- Pavlo **Followed up** with a docs pass that realigns the root README after that merge and preserves the historical replay, so the project's entry point stays accurate without erasing how earlier iterations looked. [PR #15](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/15)

### FlashProve benchmark
_The benchmark setup gained a comparability check before the real run._

- Merlini (@gobross) **Flagged** that the two suites currently prove different models, context lengths, and hardware, protecting the head-to-head from a gap that could have passed unnoticed. [tg:tawg:6443]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Shared** that their side of the FlashProve on-chain verifier is already in place as an ERC-8274 wrapper, advancing the verifiable half of the comparison. [tg:tawg:6438]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Passed along** a matching upstream failure report for the ONNX export issue, giving the debugging effort a concrete next stop instead of another blind guess. [tg:tawg:6447]

### ERC-8183
_The standards conversation moved from theory toward operational practice._

- kurosato **Brought** a data point from an escrow already running this design, grounding the thread in how it behaves in production. [ERC-8183 post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/467)
- achempers **Agreed** on both points and noted that the evaluation rule is one more consumer that needs the status at expiry, naming a concrete integration point for implementers. [ERC-8183 post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/469)

### ERC-8299
_A lingering implementation question resurfaced with fresh context._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Resurfaced** a long-running 8299 question while reading the verifier implementation, giving the group a concrete thread to inspect rather than a vague concern. [tg:tawg:6444]

### daily-bot diagnostics
_Bot delivery observability gained a small, useful step._

- Jimmy Shi **Drafted** a diagnostics-only change covering reply preparation failures and invalid Telegram mentions, making delivery problems easier to trace for everyone who depends on the daily loop. [PR #18](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/18)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Whether status at expiry should become a shared expectation across escrow designs now that a live deployment has weighed in.
- What the resurfaced 8299 question implies for the verifier interface assumptions the group is carrying.
- How the two benchmark sides can be lined up on equal model, context, and hardware footing before any published comparison.
- Whether the preserved historical replay approach is worth reusing when other repositories consolidate research branches.

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Align the FlashProve comparison inputs so both sides run under the same conditions before the head-to-head.
- Try the suggested upstream lead against the ONNX export failure and report what matches.
- Review the refreshed README and integration notes for anything the next research pass should carry forward.
- Watch the diagnostics output from the daily bot to confirm reply failures and invalid mentions are easier to pin down.

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A quiet mismatch was caught before the head-to-head — nothing flashy, just the kind of save that keeps a comparison honest.
>
> Keep flagging the wobbly bits early; every sturdy relay is a pile of quiet saves 🧭
